why: S3 object-created event notifications can invoke a Lambda function directly for each upload. Lambda scales automatically from a few invocations an hour to hundreds of concurrent ones, the sub-5-second job fits well inside the 15-minute limit, and you pay only per invocation. That makes it the most cost-effective event-driven design for spiky, unpredictable upload volumes.

others.A: CloudTrail is for auditing API calls, not for triggering processing, and AppSync is a GraphQL API service, not a file processor.
others.C: Kinesis Data Streams adds shard costs and complexity, and the files are already landing in S3, so a stream is unnecessary.
others.D: SNS cannot process files itself; adding it between S3 and Lambda only adds an extra hop when S3 can invoke Lambda directly.

tip: S3 upload plus short processing usually means an S3 event notification invoking Lambda.

why: Production runs constantly, so a Compute Savings Plan gives up to about 66% off for a 1- or 3-year commitment and stays flexible across instance family, Region and even Lambda, which the app also uses. Nonproduction runs only on weekday business hours, so On-Demand Instances that are stopped outside those hours avoid paying for idle capacity, unlike a commitment.

others.A: On-Demand for steady production wastes the commitment discount, and Dedicated Hosts are expensive and unnecessary.
others.B: Reserved Instances for nonproduction are billed 24/7 whether the instances run or not, so shutting them down saves nothing.
others.D: Dedicated Hosts for production are costly with no stated licensing need, and an Instance Savings Plan commitment is wasted on part-time nonproduction use.

tip: Use a commitment (RI or Savings Plan) for steady 24/7 load and On-Demand that you stop when idle for part-time load. Compute Savings Plans also cover Lambda and Fargate.

why: Moving from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous migration, so AWS SCT converts the schema. AWS DMS then does a full load plus change data capture (CDC) to replicate ongoing changes over the existing VPN. The requirement to capture changes during the migration is what CDC delivers.

others.A: A full-load-only DMS task does not capture changes made during the migration.
others.B: DataSync copies files, not live database changes, so it gives no CDC or schema conversion.
others.D: Snowball is an offline bulk transfer with no ongoing change capture, and it is not needed when a VPN exists.

tip: Heterogeneous migration means SCT plus DMS. The phrase 'ongoing changes' means a DMS full load plus CDC.

why: AWS Fargate is serverless compute for containers, so there are no EC2 worker nodes to patch or scale. Both ECS on Fargate and EKS on Fargate run Docker containers as a managed service, and each service scales in and out on its own (for ECS, through Service Auto Scaling).

others.C: Lambda can run container images but is not a general host for long-running Docker services, and API Gateway adds unrelated components.
others.D: ECS on EC2 means managing and scaling the EC2 container instances yourself, which is extra infrastructure.
others.E: EKS with EC2 worker nodes requires managing node groups, which adds operational overhead.

tip: 'No infrastructure to manage' for containers usually means Fargate (with ECS or EKS).

why: An Auto Scaling group with dynamic scaling adds instances only as traffic grows and removes them afterwards, so you pay for peak capacity only while it is needed. A launch template that points to a preconfigured AMI lets new instances boot quickly, ready to serve, during sudden spikes.

others.A: Keeping a full peak-sized fleet, even partly stopped, still pays for EBS volumes and means manual work. It is not a normal scaling design.
others.B: Setting the minimum size for peak traffic means paying for peak capacity all the time, which is not cost-effective.
others.C: Scaling in once caches are 'fully populated' does not work for dynamic content that changes, and it adds ElastiCache cost and complexity.

tip: Cost-effective elasticity means dynamic scaling from a golden AMI, not over-provisioning.

why: AWS Config has a managed rule, restricted-ssh (INCOMING_SSH_DISABLED), that checks security groups for SSH open to 0.0.0.0/0. It is ready to use immediately, and compliance-change events can go to SNS through EventBridge. Nothing has to be written or maintained, which matches 'as soon as possible' and 'least operational overhead'.

others.A: A custom Lambda monitor must be written, scheduled and maintained, which is more overhead than a managed rule.
others.C: Watching role assumption does not detect the actual rule, and creating a role that can open security groups globally works against the goal.
others.D: An SCP blocking security group edits plus a ticketing process is heavy-handed and manual, and it does not detect existing breaches.

tip: For compliance detection with notification, look for an AWS Config managed rule plus SNS/EventBridge.

why: Amazon VPC Lattice is built for service-to-service connectivity across accounts and VPCs. It provides a service network, HTTP/HTTPS listeners, targets that can be Lambda, EKS/IP or instances, and a built-in service directory for discovery. Sharing it through AWS RAM avoids managing peering, transit gateways or many endpoints, so it has the least administrative overhead.

others.A: An inspection VPC with Network Firewall and a transit gateway controls traffic but provides no service registry and is heavy to operate.
others.C: An NLB plus a PrivateLink endpoint service per microservice, with endpoints in every consumer VPC, does not scale well administratively and has no service discovery.
others.D: VPC peering meshes with prefix lists and route tables are manual, do not scale, and provide no service registry.

tip: Cross-account microservice connectivity with service discovery points to VPC Lattice.

why: ElastiCache for Redis (now also Valkey) sits in front of RDS as a cache with sub-millisecond reads for metadata. It also supports snapshots/backups and replication, with replicas and Multi-AZ failover. It meets all three stated capabilities without migrating the database.

others.A: Aurora Replicas improve read scale but give millisecond latency, not sub-millisecond, and the metrics say scaling the database will not help.
others.B: Migrating to DynamoDB global tables is a big re-architecture. DynamoDB alone is single-digit milliseconds, and global replication is not needed.
others.D: Memcached has no snapshot/backup or replication support.

tip: Redis vs Memcached: if the question needs snapshots, replication, persistence or advanced data types, choose Redis.

why: An AMI can be shared with an organizational unit by adding the OU ARN to its launch permissions. Because the backing snapshots are encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, the key policy must also let principals in that OU use the key (for example kms:Decrypt and kms:CreateGrant, often scoped with aws:PrincipalOrgPaths). Without this, launches fail.

others.B: Sharing with the organization root ARN shares the AMI with the whole organization, not just the development OU, which grants too much access.
others.D: Adding individual account ARNs works but must be repeated for each account. The requirement is to share with the OU.
others.E: There is no need to recreate the key, and granting the whole organization root is broader than the development OU.

tip: Sharing encrypted AMIs takes two things: launch permissions and KMS key access. The default aws/ebs key cannot be shared.

why: 80 PB at 1-2 Gbps per office would take months over the internet, missing the 4-week deadline. Several Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices per office (about 80-210 TB each) can be loaded in parallel and shipped, which is the cost-effective offline option for data spread across many sites.

others.A: Ordering 80 Direct Connect connections at 10 Gbps takes weeks to months to provision and is very expensive for a one-time move.
others.C: AWS Snowmobile has been discontinued, and one truck could not serve 80 globally distributed offices anyway.
others.D: Volume Gateway still sends data over the limited internet links, so it cannot move 1 PB per office in 4 weeks.

tip: Work out transfer time first (1 PB at 1 Gbps is roughly 93 days). If it misses the deadline, use the Snow Family.

why: An EFS file system policy is a resource-based IAM policy. Denying elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite (and ClientRootAccess if needed) to the EC2 instance roles enforces read-only access at the service using IAM authorization when clients mount with IAM. This meets the requirement to use IAM access control.

others.A: A read-only mount is a client-side setting that the application or OS could change. It is not IAM-based control.
others.C: Identity policies attach to principals, not to the file system. As worded, this is not a valid way to attach a policy to EFS.
others.D: POSIX permissions through access points are file-system level, not IAM access control, and they are more work per application.

tip: For EFS, IAM authorization uses ClientMount, ClientWrite and ClientRootAccess in the file system (resource) policy.

why: A cross-account IAM role with a trust policy naming the vendor's account or role, ideally with an external ID, lets the vendor's tool assume temporary credentials limited to the attached policies. No long-term credentials are shared, which is the most secure pattern for third-party access.

others.B: An IAM user with a password creates long-term credentials that must be shared and rotated, which is less secure.
others.C: IAM groups can only contain users from the same account. You cannot add another account's user.
others.D: Permissions boundaries limit an identity's maximum permissions; they do not allow another account to use a user. This still relies on long-term user credentials.

tip: Third-party or cross-account access means an IAM role with a trust policy and an external ID.

why: Cost allocation tags (for example owner or department) make spending traceable to each department once they are activated in Billing. AWS Budgets can then track costs against a budget, with an alert threshold at 60% that notifies the CFO by email or SNS.

others.B: Cost Explorer forecasts do not identify owners, and Cost Anomaly Detection alerts on unusual spend patterns, not a percentage of a budget.
others.C: Trusted Advisor and the Support API do not provide budget threshold alerts.
others.D: Cost Explorer forecasts cannot determine who owns resources; tags are needed for accountability.

tip: Notification at X% of budget means AWS Budgets. Per-department accountability means cost allocation tags.

why: An internal ALB in private subnets can be reached only from inside the VPC, including the office over the Site-to-Site VPN. Limiting its security group inbound rule to the office CIDR restricts access further. NAT gateways in public subnets, with an internet gateway, give the private instances outbound-only internet access to download patches.

others.A: A public ALB open to 0.0.0.0/0 exposes the app to the internet, which breaks the office-only requirement.
others.C: NAT gateways must be in public subnets. Setting only outbound rules on the ALB security group does not restrict who can reach it.
others.D: A public ALB with outbound 0.0.0.0/0 does not restrict inbound access to the office.

tip: Private app with outbound patching means private subnets plus a NAT gateway in a public subnet. Office-only access means an internal ALB over VPN or Direct Connect.

why: Amazon QLDB is a fully managed ledger database with an immutable, append-only journal that is cryptographically verifiable using SHA-256 hash chaining. It matches the requirement for verifiable logs of data changes with minimal operations.

others.A: Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics and has no immutable, verifiable change history.
others.B: Neptune is a graph database and does not provide a cryptographically verifiable journal.
others.C: Timestream is a time-series database for metrics and IoT, not a verifiable ledger.

tip: Immutable, cryptographically verifiable history points to QLDB on the exam. In practice QLDB reached end of support in July 2025; AWS suggests Aurora PostgreSQL with audit tables instead.

why: AWS Glue DataBrew provides managed, visual data preparation jobs. An AWS Step Functions state machine can orchestrate them with Parallel states for concurrent jobs and sequential states for ordered ones, plus built-in Retry/Catch error handling and state management. Running the state machine on a schedule meets the regular-interval requirement.

others.A: Chaining Lambda functions yourself leaves error handling, retries and state tracking to custom code.
others.B: Athena queries scheduled by EventBridge offer no orchestration of ordered steps or retry and state handling.
others.D: AWS Data Pipeline is in maintenance mode, and a single midnight run does not meet the parallel and ordered requirements.

tip: Removing error handling, retry logic and state management usually means Step Functions.

why: SQS FIFO queues provide exactly-once processing: within the 5-minute deduplication interval, duplicate messages are dropped using a content-based or explicit MessageDeduplicationId. A Lambda function polling the FIFO queue processes each payment once, in order per message group, which prevents duplicate payment processing.

others.A: S3 event notifications are delivered at least once and can occasionally be duplicated, so they do not guarantee no duplicates.
others.B: SQS Standard queues offer at-least-once delivery, so the same payment could be processed twice.
others.D: DynamoDB Streams with Lambda can retry batches, and nothing deduplicates payments that are inserted twice.

tip: 'No duplicates' or 'exactly-once' means SQS FIFO. Making the consumer idempotent is still best practice.

why: AWS Application Discovery Service collects server configuration, utilization and dependency data from on-premises environments, either agentless through the Agentless Collector or with the Discovery Agent. Its data is stored in the AWS Migration Hub home Region for migration planning. This directly meets the 'collect usage and configuration data' requirement.

others.A: Systems Manager manages servers but is not the migration discovery tool, and it requires the SSM agent and hybrid activation on every server.
others.C: SCT converts database schemas, and Trusted Advisor checks AWS accounts, not on-premises servers.
others.D: SCT and DMS are database migration tools and do not inventory on-premises servers.

tip: Discovering on-premises servers before migration means Application Discovery Service plus the Migration Hub home Region.

why: AWS Control Tower must be set up from the Organizations management account. It creates a landing zone with an organization-wide CloudTrail trail that audits API calls and logins in all existing and new enrolled accounts. Account Factory provisions new compliant accounts, and Security Hub with the FSBP standard reports noncompliant accounts, all as managed services with little overhead.

others.B: Control Tower cannot be launched from a member account; it must be deployed in the management account.
others.C: AMS Accelerate is an operations service with added cost, and GuardDuty detects threats but does not check FSBP compliance.
others.D: AMS adds cost and a request-for-change (RFC) process, which is more overhead and expense than Control Tower plus Security Hub.

tip: Control Tower always runs from the management account. FSBP compliance is reported by Security Hub.

why: Amazon Athena is serverless and runs SQL directly on Parquet data in S3, charging only for data scanned. Columnar Parquet keeps scans small. A Glue crawler fills in the Data Catalog table metadata. For occasional queries there is nothing to keep running, so this is the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Migrating 10 TB into Aurora means paying for a database running constantly and running a DMS migration, all for occasional queries.
others.B: Redshift Spectrum needs a Redshift cluster (or Serverless) to be provisioned, which costs more than Athena for occasional use.
others.D: An EMR cluster with Spark SQL needs cluster management and compute costs, which is too much for ad hoc SQL.

tip: Occasional SQL on data in S3 means Athena (plus the Glue Data Catalog).

why: AWS Control Tower proactive controls are implemented as CloudFormation Hooks. They check resources before CloudFormation provisions them and block noncompliant ones, for example IAM policies with inline policies or wildcards, and EC2 instances with public IPs. This prevents the deployments rather than detecting them afterwards.

others.B: Detective controls (AWS Config rules) only flag noncompliance after resources exist; they do not block deployment.
others.C: Config rules with remediation react after the fact, and Session Manager is a shell-access tool, not a remediation mechanism.
others.D: SCPs act on API actions and some condition keys and cannot easily inspect policy document contents such as inline policies with '*'. They are also not CloudFormation-aware.

tip: In Control Tower: preventive means SCPs, detective means Config rules, and proactive means CloudFormation Hooks that block before provisioning.

why: An EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones in private subnets gives scalability and high availability without code changes. An internet-facing Application Load Balancer in public subnets spreads web traffic across the healthy instances in the group.

others.A: A bigger instance is still a single point of failure in one AZ, so it is not highly available.
others.C: A NAT gateway only provides outbound internet access for private resources; it cannot serve inbound web requests.
others.D: Vertical scaling to a memory-optimized instance still leaves one instance in one AZ, with no high availability.

tip: High availability and scalability without a rewrite means an ALB plus a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group.

why: Lambda environment variables are encrypted at rest with KMS. Using a customer managed KMS key with the console's encryption helpers encrypts values client-side before they are stored. Developers who lack kms:Decrypt on the key see only ciphertext, while the function decrypts at runtime.

others.A: Moving to EC2 does not solve the visibility problem and adds operational burden.
others.B: Lambda environment variables cannot be encrypted with SSL or CloudHSM; SSL/TLS protects data in transit.
others.C: ACM certificates are for TLS and cannot be used to encrypt Lambda environment variables.

tip: For truly secret values, Secrets Manager or Parameter Store SecureString is often preferred, but KMS encryption helpers are the direct answer here.

why: An Amazon Cognito user pool is a managed user directory that handles sign-up, sign-in and token issuance and scales to millions of users. API Gateway REST APIs support a native Cognito user pool authorizer that validates the tokens without custom code, which gives the most operational efficiency.

others.B: Identity pools issue temporary AWS credentials rather than authenticating users as a user directory, and HTTP APIs use a JWT authorizer rather than a 'Cognito authorizer'.
others.C: A custom Lambda authentication service and Lambda authorizer must be built and maintained.
others.D: IAM users cannot be created for millions of end users and are not meant for customer authentication.

tip: End-user authentication for APIs means a Cognito user pool. AWS credentials for end users means a Cognito identity pool.

why: An EventBridge rule matching the KMS deletion API call (recorded by CloudTrail) can start a Systems Manager Automation runbook that calls CancelKeyDeletion during the 7-30 day waiting period, and also publish to an SNS topic that emails administrators. Both actions use managed services with no custom code.

others.A: An AWS Config rule is not a valid EventBridge target and cannot cancel key deletion.
others.B: A custom Lambda function plus a CloudWatch alarm adds code and components, which is more overhead than a managed runbook.
others.D: A CloudTrail metric filter and alarm only notifies administrators; it does not prevent the deletion.

tip: In reality the API is ScheduleKeyDeletion, and KMS keys always have a 7-30 day pending-deletion window in which deletion can be cancelled.

why: Each report finishes in under 10 minutes, within Lambda's 15-minute limit. Lambda starts immediately and runs many reports in parallel, and you pay only for execution time. For rare, bursty use it avoids paying for idle EC2 for a whole week and gives the fastest turnaround.

others.A: Running On-Demand instances continuously all week pays for idle time between requests.
others.C: ECS tasks start more slowly and need cluster and task setup, and 'schedule when requested' is awkward compared with event-driven Lambda.
others.D: Spot Instances can be interrupted, and running them continuously still pays for idle capacity.

tip: Short (under 15 minutes), infrequent, on-demand jobs suit Lambda.

why: Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) gives EC2 instances OS-bypass, low-latency, high-throughput networking for tightly coupled MPI workloads, which is the networking optimization. FSx for Lustre with scratch storage provides a high-performance parallel file system for HPC at low cost, which is the storage optimization.

others.A: Global Accelerator speeds up internet traffic from users to applications, not node-to-node HPC traffic.
others.C: CloudFront is a CDN for content delivery and does nothing for HPC cluster performance.
others.E: Elastic Beanstalk is for deploying web applications, not for tuning HPC networking or storage.

tip: For HPC, EFA handles networking, FSx for Lustre handles storage, and cluster placement groups help latency.

why: Amazon Rekognition image moderation (DetectModerationLabels) detects unsafe or unwanted content in photos with pretrained models, so no ML training is required. A Lambda function exposed through a function URL lets the web app check each upload before accepting it.

others.A: SageMaker Autopilot trains a model, which the requirement rules out.
others.C: Comprehend analyzes text, not images, and CloudFront Functions cannot call other AWS services.
others.D: Rekognition Video is for video streams and files; photos use the Rekognition Image API.

tip: Image or video moderation without training means Rekognition. Text analysis means Comprehend.

why: The root user can have up to 8 MFA devices registered, including FIDO security keys, virtual and hardware TOTP devices. Registering more than one, kept securely, means losing a single device does not lock the company out of root.

others.A: A backup administrator account cannot sign in as root or perform root-only tasks, so root access would still be lost.
others.C: Creating an admin account after losing root access does not restore root access, and you may not be able to create one without access.
others.D: An IAM user with AdministratorAccess still cannot perform root-only tasks or recover root MFA.

tip: AWS supports multiple MFA devices (up to 8) for root and IAM users.

why: An SNS topic fans out each published message to all subscribers. Partners subscribe with HTTP/HTTPS endpoints, and SNS handles delivery retries. Adding hundreds of partners a day only means adding subscriptions, with no code changes, so it has the least implementation effort and scales well.

others.A: A Timestream list plus custom Lambda delivery code means building your own fan-out and retry logic, and Timestream is a time-series database, not a registry.
others.C: A Step Functions task per partner requires editing the state machine for every new partner, which does not scale.
others.D: Kinesis Data Streams needs custom producers and consumers and is not a partner registry or HTTP push mechanism.

tip: Push to many HTTP endpoints (pub/sub fan-out) means SNS.

why: Amazon Comprehend is a managed NLP service that needs no ML expertise. Entity detection, or custom entity recognition trained only on labelled examples rather than ML code, can extract ingredient names from text. An S3 event notification invoking Lambda on each upload is the simplest, pay-per-use way to process each file.

others.B: Amazon Forecast does time-series forecasting, not text extraction.
others.C: Polly converts text to speech, and manual listening by staff is slow and costly, not an automated solution.
others.D: SageMaker requires ML knowledge to build, train and host a model, and endpoints cost more.

tip: Text understanding means Comprehend, images mean Rekognition, documents or OCR mean Textract, and forecasting means Forecast.

why: Lambda can mount an EFS file system in another account when the function's VPC has network connectivity to the EFS mount targets, for example through VPC peering, plus suitable file system policy permissions. Peering has no hourly charge, and EFS scales automatically as files are added, so this is the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Copying to a second EFS with DataSync doubles storage costs and creates ongoing sync work.
others.C: A second Lambda proxying file access doubles invocations, adds latency and complicates file access.
others.D: Lambda layers are limited to 250 MB unzipped, are static, and cannot grow as files are added.

tip: Cross-account or cross-VPC EFS access needs network connectivity (peering or Transit Gateway) plus mount target DNS/IP resolution.

why: The company must manage keys outside AWS, so client-side encryption in its own data center before upload is required for data at rest. Uploading over HTTPS (TLS), enforced by a bucket policy with aws:SecureTransport, covers encryption in transit. AWS never has the keys.

others.A: A KMS customer managed key is still managed inside AWS KMS (even with imported material), not outside the AWS Cloud.
others.B: AWS managed KMS keys are fully controlled by AWS.
others.C: Default SSE-S3 uses keys owned and managed by S3.

tip: Keys must stay outside AWS means client-side encryption (or SSE-C, or an XKS external key store).

why: API Gateway receives mobile requests, and a Lambda integration does the lightweight validation serverlessly. The long-running backend runs on ECS with Fargate, where task CPU and memory can be adjusted without managing servers. Everything is managed, so operational overhead is lowest.

others.A: EventBridge rules cannot run validation logic, and EKS Anywhere means running your own on-premises Kubernetes infrastructure.
others.B: EKS with self-managed nodes requires managing EC2 worker nodes, and Step Functions is heavier than needed for simple validation.
others.C: Spot Instances can be interrupted and must be managed, which does not suit long-running payment processing, and EventBridge cannot validate.

tip: Long-running containers with adjustable CPU and memory and no infrastructure to manage means ECS on Fargate.

why: Amazon Cognito user pools scale to millions of users. Their threat protection (advanced security) feature provides risk-based adaptive authentication, which scores each sign-in on signals such as new device, location or IP address and can require MFA only for risky attempts. That matches 'invoke 2FA for inconsistent locations, IPs or devices'.

others.B: Identity pools federate identities into AWS credentials; they do not authenticate users or do adaptive MFA.
others.C: IAM users are for workforce access to AWS, not millions of application users, and there is no risk-based MFA.
others.D: IAM Identity Center is for workforce SSO into AWS accounts and apps, not for customer-scale app authentication with adaptive risk checks.

tip: 'Adaptive' or 'risk-based' MFA for app users points to Cognito user pool threat protection.

why: AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service for the daily transform and load. Amazon Redshift Serverless provides an MPP data warehouse without clusters to manage. Redshift ML lets analysts create and train models with SQL CREATE MODEL statements, using SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. This is the all-serverless combination that meets every requirement.

others.A: EMR and provisioned Redshift both involve managing clusters, which breaks the 'serverless wherever possible' requirement.
others.B: Aurora is an OLTP database, not an MPP warehouse, and Aurora ML calls existing models rather than training them with SQL.
others.D: Athena is a query engine, not a data warehouse you load data into. Athena ML only invokes SageMaker endpoints; it does not train models.

tip: SQL-based ML training means Redshift ML. Serverless ETL means Glue.

why: AWS Outposts racks bring AWS infrastructure and services, including EKS (local or extended clusters), EC2, EBS and S3 on Outposts, into the customer's own data center. Data stays on premises for compliance while the company uses AWS managed services.

others.A: Local Zones are AWS-operated sites in metro areas, not inside the customer's data center, so data would sit in a remote site.
others.B: Snowmobile was a data transfer truck (now discontinued), not a platform for running EKS.
others.D: Snowball Edge is mainly for data transfer or limited edge compute and does not provide managed EKS for ongoing production use.

tip: AWS services in your own data center with data residency on premises means Outposts.

why: S3 File Gateway presents NFS (or SMB) shares to existing workloads and stores the files as objects in Amazon S3, which scales without limit. S3 Lifecycle policies can then move older data to cheaper storage classes. Pairing the NFS interface with low-cost S3 storage makes it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Volume Gateway provides iSCSI block volumes, not NFS file shares, and its data is stored as EBS snapshots that S3 Lifecycle policies cannot tier.
others.C: EFS storage costs more per GB than S3, and these options do not address how on-premises workloads would reach EFS.
others.D: EFS One Zone-IA is cheaper than EFS Standard but still costs more than S3 tiers, and it has single-AZ durability risk.

tip: On-premises NFS or SMB backed by cheap, scalable S3 storage means S3 File Gateway.

why: For CPU-intensive Lambda code, more memory also means proportionally more vCPU, so runs are shorter. Billing is memory times duration, so the right-sized memory recommended by Compute Optimizer can lower cost overall. Provisioned concurrency keeps environments initialized to avoid cold starts during events, preserving latency, and its lower per-GB-second duration rate helps when it is highly used.

others.A: Reserved concurrency only caps or guarantees concurrency and can cause throttling, and less memory slows CPU-bound code.
others.B: Reserved concurrency does nothing for cold-start latency and can throttle during growing events.
others.C: Decreasing memory cuts CPU, increasing duration and latency for CPU-bound code.

tip: Lambda CPU scales with memory. Provisioned concurrency avoids cold starts, while reserved concurrency limits or guarantees capacity.

why: ECS pulls images natively from Amazon ECR, so moving images to ECR needs only a change to the image URI. ECR basic scanning with scan-on-push filters scans new images for CVEs automatically, and existing images can be scanned on demand. This is the fewest changes to the workloads.

others.B: Macie finds sensitive data in S3, not software vulnerabilities, and ECS does not run images from S3.
others.C: Migrating the workloads to EKS is a major change, which breaks the 'fewest changes' requirement.
others.D: Container images are not stored in or run from S3 for ECS, and Inspector does not scan S3 objects as container images.

tip: Container CVE scanning means ECR image scanning: basic (Clair/AWS native) or enhanced (Inspector).

why: AWS Batch sends job state-change events, including SUCCEEDED, to EventBridge by default. An EventBridge rule can target an API destination, which uses an EventBridge connection storing Basic auth (username and password) in Secrets Manager. It calls the third-party HTTP API serverlessly with no code.

others.B: EventBridge Scheduler runs schedules; it does not match incoming events. A Lambda function also adds code that is not needed.
others.C: Batch jobs do not natively publish events to API Gateway, and this adds unnecessary components.
others.D: This adds API Gateway and Lambda code, and Batch does not publish to API Gateway on its own.

tip: Calling an external HTTP API from an event without code means an EventBridge API destination.

why: With no internet gateway, VPN or Direct Connect, AWS PrivateLink gives private access across accounts. The vendor puts an NLB in front of the RDS instance (using its IP as a target) and publishes a VPC endpoint service. The company creates an interface endpoint to it, and traffic stays on the AWS network with no route-table or CIDR coupling.

others.A: The Direct Connect hosted connection program is for on-premises connectivity and is irrelevant between two VPCs.
others.B: Client VPN is for individual users connecting to a VPC, not a VPC-to-VPC link.
others.D: Transit Gateway and VPC peering together are redundant, and either one needs route and CIDR coordination with the vendor. PrivateLink exposes only the one service.

tip: Expose one service privately to another account or VPC means PrivateLink (an NLB endpoint service).

why: Amazon Managed Grafana workspaces can be configured with VPC outbound connectivity to reach data sources in private subnets. Connecting to the RDS instance's private endpoint keeps traffic inside the VPC and never exposes the database to the internet.

others.A: A public RDS endpoint exposes the database over the internet.
others.C: RDS databases are not exposed as AWS PrivateLink endpoint services for Grafana to use this way. Grafana needs VPC connectivity to reach a private DB.
others.D: Using a public RDS endpoint again exposes data over the internet, even if the workspace is in a VPC.

tip: For private data sources, connect Managed Grafana to the VPC instead of making the database public.

why: AWS Glue DataBrew is a no-code visual data preparation tool with over 250 prebuilt transformations, such as filtering anomalies and normalizing dates. It provides data profiling and data lineage views. Transformation steps are saved as reusable, shareable recipes, with outputs written to S3.

others.A: Glue Studio jobs generate code-based ETL and do not provide DataBrew-style profiling or shareable recipe steps.
others.B: EMR Serverless needs Spark or Hive code and has no built-in profiling or lineage.
others.D: Athena SQL queries require writing code and offer no data profiling or lineage.

tip: No-code data preparation with profiling, lineage and recipes means Glue DataBrew.

why: A Route 53 alias A record for the development hostname pointing at the ALB, plus a host-header listener rule that forwards that hostname to the dev instance's target group, routes engineers correctly. A replacement instance only needs to be registered in that target group, for example by an Auto Scaling group, so DNS never changes.

others.B: A record pointing at an instance's public IP breaks when the instance is replaced and its IP changes.
others.C: ALB redirect actions go to a hostname or URL, and redirecting to a public IP breaks when the instance is replaced.
others.D: Putting all instances in one target group means the listener rule cannot single out the development instance.

tip: Route by hostname to different backends means ALB host-based routing rules to separate target groups.

why: The app already runs on Kubernetes and uses AMQP. Amazon EKS lets the same manifests run on managed Kubernetes, and Amazon MQ (ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ) supports AMQP natively, so no code changes are needed. Both are managed services, which minimizes operational overhead.

others.A: SQS does not speak AMQP, so the application would have to be rewritten, and moving from Kubernetes to ECS means redoing the deployments.
others.C: Self-managed EC2 instances mean operating servers yourself, which is more overhead than EKS.
others.D: Rewriting to Lambda and SQS needs significant code changes and drops AMQP support.

tip: Existing protocols such as AMQP, MQTT, STOMP or JMS mean Amazon MQ. Existing Kubernetes means EKS.

why: AWS Global Accelerator gives two static anycast IPs that bring players onto the AWS global network at the nearest edge location, then route over AWS's backbone to the closest healthy NLB endpoint in each Region. It cuts latency and jitter for TCP/UDP gaming traffic and supports NLBs as endpoints.

others.A: ALBs are Layer 7 and handle only HTTP/HTTPS, which does not suit game traffic, and swapping load balancers does not reduce global latency.
others.B: Equal weighted routing ignores user location and can send players to far-away Regions.
others.C: More Regions may help some users but is costly and still lacks smart routing to the nearest endpoint.

tip: Non-HTTP (TCP/UDP) global performance with static IPs means Global Accelerator. HTTP caching means CloudFront.

why: AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed SFTP (also FTPS, FTP, AS2) endpoint that stores uploads directly in Amazon S3. Legacy vendors keep their SFTP clients and the company runs no servers.

others.A: DMS migrates databases; it is not an SFTP upload service for vendors.
others.C: A self-managed EC2 SFTP server needs patching, scaling and HA work, which is more overhead.
others.D: S3 File Gateway exposes SMB or NFS, not SFTP, and needs a gateway appliance.

tip: Managed SFTP into S3 or EFS means AWS Transfer Family.

why: Textract extracts the text from the PDF reports. Amazon Comprehend, a managed NLP service, then performs sentiment analysis plus key phrase and entity extraction to give content insights. Results are saved to S3 with no model building, which keeps overhead lowest.

others.A: Athena queries structured data with SQL; it cannot perform sentiment analysis on text.
others.B: Building a custom SageMaker sentiment model adds major overhead when Comprehend does this out of the box.
others.D: QuickSight visualizes data but does not derive sentiment from raw text.

tip: Textract to Comprehend is the standard pipeline for document OCR followed by NLP or sentiment.

why: Kinesis Data Streams ingests real-time data from third-party producers. Amazon Data Firehose, which can use a data stream as its source, buffers the records and delivers them to an S3 bucket with no custom consumers, landing raw data in S3 as required.

others.B: DMS migrates databases and cannot ingest arbitrary real-time application data.
others.C: DataSync moves files between storage systems in batches; it does not ingest real-time streams.
others.D: Direct Connect is a private link to on-premises networks and is irrelevant for third-party application data ingestion.

tip: Real-time ingestion landing in S3 means Kinesis Data Streams and/or Firehose. Firehose alone often suffices.

why: DynamoDB items are limited to 400 KB, and the data is already 700 KB and growing. The standard pattern stores the payload in S3, which allows objects up to 50 TB, and keeps a DynamoDB item with metadata and the S3 key or URL. This scales with no custom size-handling logic.

others.A: Running a second database (DocumentDB) and splitting logic across stores adds operational complexity.
others.C: Chunking data across items requires custom reassembly, BatchWriteItem is not atomic, and it is limited to 25 items and 16 MB.
others.D: Compression may not keep growing data under 400 KB, and it adds processing overhead.

tip: DynamoDB item limit is 400 KB. For large payloads, store them in S3 and keep a pointer in DynamoDB.

why: EventBridge Scheduler supports cron, rate and one-time schedules at scale and can launch ECS tasks on Fargate directly. Containerizing the existing cron scripts needs minimal refactoring, and Fargate has no 15-minute limit, so 1-20 minute jobs run reliably. One-time schedules cover running a job at a future time.

others.A: Lambda's 15-minute maximum timeout cannot handle jobs that run up to 20 minutes.
others.B: AWS Batch scheduling policies control fair-share job ordering, not time-based cron triggers.
others.D: Building Step Functions workflows with Wait states for hundreds of cron jobs is cumbersome and costly compared with Scheduler.

tip: Jobs over 15 minutes cannot run on Lambda. Use EventBridge Scheduler with ECS on Fargate for containerized cron.

why: Amazon AppFlow is a no-code SaaS integration service with a native Salesforce connector. It supports full and incremental (change) transfers into Redshift. AppFlow can use AWS PrivateLink to Salesforce so data does not travel over the public internet, giving the least development effort.

others.A: You cannot set up a VPN to Salesforce's SaaS platform this way, and DataBrew is a data preparation tool, not a Salesforce ingestion service.
others.B: Direct Connect to Salesforce is not a standard option, and DataBrew still does not handle ongoing Salesforce change ingestion.
others.D: You cannot peer a VPC with Salesforce, because peering works only between AWS VPCs.

tip: SaaS (Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk) to AWS with no code means AppFlow.

why: S3 storage costs much less than EFS, and S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent, infrequent and archive instant access tiers based on usage, with no retrieval fees. The question allows 'some application changes', so switching the app to the S3 API in exchange for the lowest storage cost is acceptable.

others.B: FSx for Windows File Server costs more and needs a protocol change to SMB/CIFS for Linux apps, so it does not save money.
others.C: FSx for OpenZFS uses provisioned capacity and generally costs more than S3 for this use.
others.D: Glacier Flexible Retrieval takes minutes to hours to retrieve files, which is unsuitable for an application that reads files on demand.

tip: Unknown or changing access patterns with the lowest cost means S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

why: Only the Application Load Balancer (Layer 7) supports listener rules that route on query string parameters, as well as path, host and headers, to different target groups. An HTTPS listener with an ACM certificate gives free, auto-renewing TLS encryption.

others.A: NLBs work at Layer 4 and cannot inspect or route on query strings.
others.B: Gateway Load Balancers are for inline virtual appliances (GENEVE), do not terminate TLS, and do not do HTTP routing.
others.D: NLBs cannot do query-parameter routing, and ACM is preferred over IAM certificate storage.

tip: Any HTTP content-based routing (path, host, header, query string) means ALB.

why: An Auto Scaling group behind an ALB makes the web tier highly available across AZs and lets it scale automatically. Aurora Serverless (v2) is MySQL-compatible, scales database capacity automatically with load, and stores data across 3 AZs with failover. Both tiers become highly available and automatically scalable.

others.A: Redshift is a data warehouse, not a MySQL-compatible OLTP database.
others.B: A static target group without Auto Scaling does not scale automatically, and a provisioned RDS cluster does not auto-scale compute.
others.D: ElastiCache is a cache, not a replacement for the MySQL database, and there is no Auto Scaling for the app tier.

tip: 'Automatically scalable' relational DB often means Aurora Serverless v2.

why: A KMS customer managed key with automatic rotation enabled rotates key material yearly by default (configurable from 90 to 2560 days). Setting it as the bucket's default encryption (SSE-KMS) encrypts all migrated data with no manual rotation work. It also makes the yearly rotation verifiable.

others.A: SSE-S3 keys are fully managed by AWS, and you cannot configure or verify a yearly rotation schedule for them.
others.C: Manual rotation adds operational overhead when automatic rotation is available.
others.D: KMS keys with imported key material do not support automatic rotation, and imported material adds key management work.

tip: Automatic yearly rotation you control means a KMS customer managed key with rotation enabled. Imported material cannot auto-rotate.

why: IAM Identity Center provides SSO across all accounts in the organization. Using AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity source, with a two-way forest trust to the self-managed on-premises AD, lets users and groups stay managed on premises while Identity Center can sync them and authenticate through the trust.

others.A: A standalone Managed Microsoft AD without a trust would require recreating and managing users in AWS instead of on premises.
others.C: A Directory Service trust alone does not provide SSO across AWS accounts without IAM Identity Center.
others.D: Running a self-managed IdP on EC2 adds operational overhead and duplicates what the AD integration already offers.

tip: On-premises AD to Identity Center works through AD Connector or Managed Microsoft AD with a two-way trust.

why: Aurora I/O-Optimized removes per-request I/O charges in exchange for higher compute and storage prices. It gives predictable, better price-performance for I/O-heavy, high-traffic workloads, and AWS says it saves money once I/O exceeds about 25% of total Aurora spend. It also supports Serverless v2.

others.A: Aurora Standard charges per I/O request, which becomes expensive under heavy, growing I/O.
others.B: Provisioned IOPS is an RDS/EBS storage type, not an Aurora cluster storage option.
others.C: General Purpose (gp2/gp3) is an RDS/EBS storage type, not an Aurora option.

tip: Aurora storage choices are Standard (pay per I/O) or I/O-Optimized (no I/O charges). Choose I/O-Optimized for I/O-heavy workloads.

why: AWS Security Hub (now Security Hub CSPM) runs automated, continuous control checks against standards including NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 and PCI DSS. With a delegated administrator and Organizations integration, it aggregates compliance status across hundreds of accounts, giving auditors evidence that controls are implemented and working.

others.A: Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and network exposure; it does not evaluate NIST or PCI DSS control standards.
others.B: GuardDuty is threat detection and has no NIST or PCI DSS compliance standards.
others.C: CloudTrail records API activity and has no security standards to enable.

tip: Compliance against standards (CIS, FSBP, NIST, PCI) points to Security Hub. AWS Audit Manager is another audit-evidence option.

why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves each object between access tiers based on its own access pattern, with millisecond retrieval in the frequent, infrequent and archive instant tiers and no retrieval fees. It suits unpredictable, random access by many apps, and a single Lifecycle rule makes it the most operationally efficient choice.

others.B: Glacier objects need restores before access, so data is not immediately available, and S3 Select is being retired for new customers.
others.C: Standard-IA has retrieval fees and does not move objects back when they get busy, so random hot data costs more.
others.D: A custom Lambda function to move objects back to Standard adds code, overhead and transition costs.

tip: Random or unknown access patterns plus cost savings means Intelligent-Tiering.

why: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database that stores profiles as vertices and connections as edges. Multi-hop traversals such as mutual connections up to five levels deep run efficiently with Gremlin, openCypher or SPARQL, avoiding the exponential cost of repeated SQL self-joins.

others.A: Athena SQL with five-level self-joins over 10 million relationships would be slow and costly.
others.C: QuickSight visualizes data; it does not run graph traversal queries.
others.D: Relational multi-level JOINs over many-to-many relationships perform poorly as depth increases.

tip: Relationships, social networks or 'friends of friends' means Neptune.

why: An AWS Site-to-Site VPN can be configured in minutes over the existing internet connection. It gives an encrypted IPsec tunnel between the on-premises network and a VPC, with low hourly and data charges, which fits low bandwidth, quick setup and lowest cost.

others.A: Client VPN connects individual user devices, not a whole on-premises network, and charges per connection.
others.B: Direct Connect takes weeks to provision and is costly, which is overkill for small traffic volumes.
others.C: A bastion host provides administrative SSH or RDP access, not a network-to-network secure connection.

tip: Quick, cheap, low-bandwidth link means Site-to-Site VPN. High bandwidth or consistent performance means Direct Connect.

why: AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP endpoints backed by S3. Choosing AWS Directory Service as the identity provider, with AD Connector pointing at the on-premises AD, lets employees authenticate with their existing AD credentials over SFTP. No servers or user copies need to be managed.

others.A: S3 File Gateway provides SMB/NFS, not SFTP, so the file access mechanism would change.
others.B: A self-managed SFTP fleet on EC2 brings patching, scaling and integration overhead.
others.D: Transfer Family cannot connect directly to an on-premises AD; it needs an AWS Directory Service directory such as AD Connector or Managed Microsoft AD.

tip: Transfer Family identity providers are service-managed, AWS Directory Service (Managed AD or AD Connector), or a custom provider through Lambda or API Gateway.

why: EventBridge rules decouple producers from consumers, and each rule can target one validation Lambda. An input transformer on each target passes only the fields that function needs, enforcing least information. New validation steps are added just by adding rules, which keeps the design loosely coupled.

others.A: A custom transformer Lambda that knows every queue tightly couples the system and adds code.
others.B: SNS message filtering decides whether a subscriber gets a message; it cannot trim the payload, so each function would receive the full order.
others.D: A central Lambda making synchronous parallel calls is tightly coupled and fragile.

tip: Reshape or trim the event payload per target means an EventBridge input transformer.

why: Aurora MySQL with Aurora Replicas offloads the heavy real-time reporting reads to replicas through the reader endpoint, which load-balances across them. The writer instance then stays free for inserts, improving write performance. Multi-AZ adds high availability.

others.A: Moving reports to DynamoDB requires a major refactor and duplicating data, and it is poorly suited to ad hoc reporting.
others.B: A bigger self-managed EC2 database keeps reads and writes contending on the same instance.
others.D: A Multi-AZ standby cannot serve reads, and there is no 'backup instance' endpoint for reports.

tip: Reporting slows down writes means read replicas and a reader endpoint.

why: An S3 interface endpoint (PrivateLink) in a VPC has private IP addresses that on-premises hosts can reach over a Direct Connect private VIF. Traffic to S3 needs no internet access, and only endpoint hourly and per-GB charges apply.

others.A: A public VIF reaches all AWS public endpoints and advertises public prefixes, which is less suited to a closed network that cannot have internet-style access. It also offers less control than a private endpoint.
others.B: A NAT gateway cannot be used by on-premises traffic through Direct Connect to reach S3 (transitive routing is not supported), and it adds processing charges.
others.D: VPC peering is only between VPCs; you cannot peer an on-premises network with Direct Connect.

tip: On premises reaching S3 privately over Direct Connect or VPN means an S3 interface endpoint. Gateway endpoints are not reachable from on premises.

why: Route 53 multivalue answer routing returns up to eight healthy records chosen at random. Associating Route 53 health checks with each Region's endpoint spreads traffic across both Regions and stops returning an unhealthy Region, meeting both the growth and DR requirements.

others.A: Simple routing does not support health checks, so it could keep sending users to an unhealthy Region.
others.C: An ALB target group cannot register EC2 instance IDs from another Region.
others.D: Cross-Region IP targets would need private connectivity, and a single-Region ALB is itself a single point of failure for DR.

tip: Health checks work with failover, weighted, latency, geolocation and multivalue routing, but not simple routing.

why: Amazon EFS is a regional, elastic NFS file system that many Linux EC2 instances across multiple AZs can mount at the same time. Large files stay available everywhere without copying between instances, and EFS scales throughput and capacity automatically.

others.A: Making employees switch to S3 changes how they access files and does not give the EC2 applications a shared file system.
others.B: EBS volumes created from snapshots are separate copies. Multi-Attach is limited to io1/io2 in a single AZ and needs a cluster-aware file system.
others.D: Instance store is ephemeral and local to each instance, so files are neither shared nor durable.

tip: Shared file storage across many Linux instances and AZs means EFS. For Windows, use FSx for Windows File Server.

why: EBS encryption and RDS encryption both use AWS KMS keys to encrypt data at rest, along with snapshots and backups, transparently. Existing unencrypted RDS instances and EBS volumes are encrypted by copying a snapshot with encryption and restoring it. This uses native features, so infrastructure changes are minimal.

others.A: ACM certificates are for TLS in transit and cannot encrypt volumes.
others.B: CloudHSM requires building and managing an HSM cluster and integrating it yourself, which is a big infrastructure change.
others.C: SSL/TLS encrypts data in transit, not at rest.

tip: At rest means KMS-based EBS, RDS or S3 encryption. In transit means TLS (ACM).

why: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint adds a route-table entry (an S3 prefix list) that sends S3 traffic from the private subnets directly to S3 over the AWS network. Traffic bypasses the saturated NAT instance and the internet, and gateway endpoints have no hourly or data charges.

others.A: A NAT gateway adds bandwidth, but S3 traffic would still go through NAT and out to the public S3 endpoint, with per-GB processing fees.
others.B: A larger NAT instance may ease saturation but still sends S3 traffic through NAT and the internet path.
others.D: A transit gateway connects VPCs and networks; it does not give private access to S3.

tip: Private and free S3 or DynamoDB access from a VPC means a gateway endpoint.

why: AWS Global Accelerator routes TCP (and UDP) traffic from the nearest edge location over the AWS global backbone to the regional endpoint, and terminates TCP close to the client. This improves throughput and reliability for RTMP streams sent by reporters worldwide.

others.A: CloudFront is mainly for delivering HTTP(S) content to viewers and does not accelerate RTMP ingest; RTMP distributions were retired.
others.C: Client VPN gives remote network access but does not accelerate connections and adds encryption overhead.
others.D: Elastic IPs give static addresses but no global network acceleration.

tip: Accelerate non-HTTP TCP/UDP traffic globally means Global Accelerator.

why: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policies can automatically move monthly snapshots to EBS Snapshots Archive and keep them for 7 years. Archive costs about 75% less than standard snapshot storage, with a 90-day minimum and 24-72 hour restores, which suits regulatory retention. Daily snapshots keep their current policy, so administrative effort is minimal.

others.A: EBS snapshots cannot be copied directly into S3 Glacier Deep Archive as an option; this needs custom export tooling.
others.C: Keeping 84 monthly snapshots in the standard tier for 7 years costs far more than the archive tier.
others.D: Building EBS direct API exports to S3 is custom work with high operational overhead.

tip: Long-term retention of EBS snapshots means EBS Snapshots Archive through Data Lifecycle Manager or AWS Backup.

why: AWS Backup is a managed service that can schedule daily EFS backups and copy each recovery point to a vault in another Region using a copy rule in the backup plan. It needs no scripts or infrastructure, which makes it a cost-effective managed cross-Region solution among the options.

others.A: The EFS-to-EFS backup solution was an older CloudFormation and Lambda solution that has been retired in favour of AWS Backup and EFS replication.
others.B: A nightly script to S3 plus cross-Region replication is custom and not a managed EFS replication approach.
others.C: Cross-Region peering with rsync scripts is self-managed and operationally heavy.

tip: Native EFS Replication now also copies a file system to another Region continuously. Among these options, AWS Backup is the managed answer.

why: An Auto Scaling group of web EC2 instances across two AZs behind an ALB scales with promotional demand and is highly available. Amazon RDS for SQL Server with Multi-AZ gives a managed database with automatic synchronous standby failover. Both tiers use managed features, so administrative overhead is lowest.

others.A: Two fixed instances without Auto Scaling cannot scale for the event, and read replicas do not give automatic write failover.
others.B: Self-managed SQL Server on EC2 across Regions with replication means heavy database administration.
others.D: Fixed instance counts do not scale, and self-managed databases on EC2 add overhead.

tip: HA plus scalable plus least admin means ASG with ALB for the app and RDS Multi-AZ for the database.

why: AWS Storage Gateway, using S3 File Gateway, presents an on-premises SMB share backed by Amazon S3 and caches data locally for low-latency access. The application keeps writing to an SMB share with no code changes, while files are copied to AWS over the existing VPN.

others.A: EFS is NFS for Linux and is hosted in AWS, so it neither provides an on-premises low-latency SMB share nor avoids changes.
others.B: FSx for Windows lives in AWS; on-premises servers would reach it over the VPN with higher latency, unless an FSx File Gateway were added.
others.C: Snowball is for one-time offline bulk transfers, not continuous daily file copies.

tip: On premises keeps using SMB or NFS while data lands in AWS means Storage Gateway (S3 or FSx File Gateway).

why: A Lambda function scheduled daily by EventBridge Scheduler or a rule can scan the small 15-item table and publish emails through SNS. It is serverless and costs almost nothing, with no servers or cron hosts to manage, which gives the most operational efficiency.

others.A: An EC2 instance running cron must be patched and kept running all the time, which is more overhead for a tiny daily task.
others.B: SQS cannot send emails, and an EC2 cron host adds overhead.
others.D: SQS is a queue and cannot deliver email to employees.

tip: Simple scheduled tasks mean an EventBridge schedule plus Lambda. Email notification means SNS (or SES for custom emails).

why: The spike happens at a known date each year, so an Auto Scaling scheduled action, recurring through a cron expression, can raise desired, minimum and maximum capacity ahead of the holiday. Capacity is ready before users arrive, which is proactive rather than reactive scaling.

others.A: A CPU alarm at 90% is reactive; it scales only after performance has already degraded.
others.C: Manually changing min and max is not automated and risks being forgotten. A scheduled action does this automatically.
others.D: SNS notifications on launches only send alerts; they do not add capacity.

tip: Known future peaks mean scheduled scaling. Recurring patterns learned from history can also use predictive scaling.

why: AWS Secrets Manager has built-in managed rotation for Amazon RDS PostgreSQL. You can turn on rotation, or let RDS manage the master user password in Secrets Manager, and it updates both the secret and the database password on a schedule with no custom code.

others.B: Parameter Store has no built-in automatic rotation for parameters.
others.C: Writing and maintaining your own rotation Lambda function is more operational overhead.
others.D: KMS key rotation rotates encryption key material, not database passwords, and KMS does not store passwords.

tip: Automatic database credential rotation means Secrets Manager.

why: Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle is a managed database that gives privileged (OS and database) access, so third-party features that need elevated access can be installed and configured. It supports BYOL for Enterprise Edition, so it keeps managed benefits while meeting the privileged-access requirement cost-effectively.

others.A: Standard RDS for Oracle does not allow privileged OS access, and replacing the features with Lambda would mean a rewrite.
others.C: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and cannot host an Oracle application or its third-party features.
others.D: Migrating to PostgreSQL and rewriting code costs significant effort and removes needed features.

tip: Managed Oracle or SQL Server with OS or privileged access means RDS Custom.

why: AWS Backup is the native, centralized service for policy-based backup plans across EC2, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS and more. It schedules, retains, monitors and reports on backups from one console and replaces the custom scripts.

others.A: Third-party software plus a tape gateway is not AWS native centralization and adds licences and complexity.
others.C: AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance; it does not take snapshots or manage backups.
others.D: State Manager enforces instance configuration; it is not a backup service for RDS or DynamoDB.

tip: Centralize or automate backups across AWS services means AWS Backup (with Organizations backup policies for many accounts).

why: An IT infrastructure map is a highly connected graph of resources and their relationships. Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database that stores this as vertices and edges and supports graph queries (SPARQL, Gremlin or openCypher). Security teams can quickly traverse relationships, such as which resources expose a risky path, with little operational overhead.

others.A: Relational SQL with many joins is cumbersome and slow for traversing complex relationships.
others.C: Redshift is an analytics warehouse, not suited to relationship traversal queries.
others.D: DynamoDB PartiQL works on key-value data and does not support graph traversal.

tip: Relationships between entities (networks, fraud, knowledge graphs, infrastructure maps) mean Neptune.

why: Aurora Serverless (v2 can scale down to 0 ACUs with auto-pause) automatically scales capacity to low developer usage and pauses or shrinks when idle, so you pay only while developers work. A Service Catalog product lets developers self-provision governed, size-limited databases.

others.A: Scripting start and stop of provisioned Aurora instances is operational work and does not match irregular working times across time zones.
others.B: Provisioned Aurora instances bill while running even when idle, which is less cost-effective than serverless.
others.D: Terminating idle databases destroys developers' data and is reactive, not a provisioning solution.

tip: Intermittent, unpredictable, low-volume database use means Aurora Serverless v2 (scale to zero).

why: Amazon EFS is a shared NFS file system that all instances in the Auto Scaling group across AZs mount at the same time. Any file a user adds or updates is visible to every instance right away, giving the least lag with no syncing.

others.A: Copying assets from the newest instance via user data is fragile, and ALBs cannot direct writes to a specific instance this way.
others.C: An hourly S3 sync means up to an hour of stale content and extra complexity.
others.D: EBS volumes restored from snapshots are point-in-time copies that do not stay in sync.

tip: Shared, always up-to-date content for many web servers means EFS.

why: Amazon GuardDuty continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and other sources to detect suspicious behaviour. Its findings go to EventBridge, where a rule can invoke Lambda to update AWS WAF rules or IP sets automatically, for example to block malicious IPs. This covers automatic detection and response.

others.B: Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall policies; it does not detect threats or produce threat findings.
others.C: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not runtime suspicious behaviour, and it does not update WAF rules.
others.D: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 and is not a general threat detection service.

tip: Suspicious or unexpected behaviour means GuardDuty. Automated response means EventBridge plus Lambda.

why: IAM database authentication for Aurora lets applications use short-lived authentication tokens (valid 15 minutes) generated with the EC2 instance role's credentials instead of static passwords. You enable it on the cluster, create a DB user with the IAM plugin, and grant rds-db:connect to the role. There are no secrets to store or rotate.

others.A: Passing static credentials as CloudFormation parameters keeps long-lived passwords around, which the requirement prohibits.
others.B: Parameter Store still holds static credentials that must be maintained and rotated.
others.D: IAM users cannot be associated with EC2 instances, and their long-term access keys are less secure than roles.

tip: No static DB credentials for EC2 or Lambda means IAM database authentication through an instance role.

why: CloudFront requires ACM certificates to be in us-east-1 (N. Virginia). ACM public certificates are free and auto-renew, so requesting a public certificate in us-east-1 for the custom domain enables HTTPS on the distribution at no extra cost.

others.A: Private certificates need AWS Private CA, which is paid, and are not trusted by public browsers.
others.B: Private certificates cost money, and CloudFront cannot use certificates from us-west-1.
others.D: CloudFront only uses ACM certificates from us-east-1.

tip: CloudFront certificates must be in us-east-1. Regional ALB certificates must be in the ALB's Region.

why: An S3 presigned URL grants temporary access to one specific object using the signer's permissions. With SigV4 it can be valid for up to 7 days when signed with IAM user credentials. The consultant gets exactly the report for the required period, with no IAM users or bucket policy changes to manage.

others.A: A public static website exposes the operations data to anyone, and migrating data is unnecessary work.
others.B: Making the bucket public exposes all data, not only the report, and it is insecure.
others.C: Creating and later revoking an IAM user with access keys is more overhead and risk than a presigned URL.

tip: Temporary access to one object for an outsider means a presigned URL (maximum 7 days with IAM user credentials; shorter with role credentials).

why: A cluster placement group packs instances close together inside one Availability Zone on a low-latency, high-bisection-bandwidth network segment. It gives the lowest latency and highest per-flow throughput for tightly coupled node-to-node HPC traffic, and EFA can be added on top.

others.B: Dedicated Instance tenancy isolates hardware for compliance or licensing; it does not improve network latency.
others.C: Spot Instances lower cost but can be interrupted, and they do not improve networking.
others.D: Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity, not network proximity or performance.

tip: Placement groups: cluster for low latency (HPC), spread for isolating critical instances, partition for large distributed systems (HDFS, Cassandra).

why: AWS's maximum resiliency model for critical workloads uses separate connections terminating on separate devices in more than one Direct Connect location, with redundancy at each site. Two connections from each data center to two locations on separate devices survive the loss of a device, a location or an entire data center.

others.A: All connections come from the primary data center only, so losing that site loses all connectivity.
others.B: A single location on the same device is a single point of failure.
others.D: A single Direct Connect location is still a single point of failure if that location goes down.

tip: Direct Connect resiliency levels: development (1 location), high (2 locations, 1 connection each), maximum (2 locations, 2 connections each on separate devices).

why: In Organizations, Trusted Advisor's organizational view in the management account aggregates check results from all member accounts, so the finance team can review everything centrally. The databases are On-Demand and highly utilized, so the Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization check shows savings from buying RIs.

others.B: Checking each member account separately works but is less efficient than the aggregated management-account view.
others.D: The instances are highly utilized, so the Idle DB Instances check will not find savings.
others.E: Compute Optimizer focuses on EC2, EBS, Lambda and similar resources. For heavily used On-Demand RDS, the RI purchase recommendation is the relevant cost lever.

tip: Steady, high-utilization On-Demand usage means buy Reserved Instances or Savings Plans.

why: An S3 gateway endpoint lets private-subnet instances reach S3 through a route-table entry, with no hourly or per-GB endpoint charges, and the traffic stays on the AWS network. This minimizes data transfer cost for frequent large-file access and keeps confidential data off the internet.

others.B: A NAT gateway charges per GB processed, which is expensive for large files, and one NAT gateway is a single AZ point of failure.
others.C: Interface endpoints charge hourly and per GB, and they use DNS rather than route-table entries.
others.D: NAT gateways in every AZ multiply the hourly and processing costs.

tip: S3 gateway endpoint is free. S3 interface endpoint is paid and is needed for on-premises or cross-Region access.

why: Amazon RDS for MySQL with Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) delivers consistent, high write IOPS for heavy import traffic. CloudWatch metrics such as WriteIOPS and WriteLatency show performance, and the provisioned IOPS can be raised when needed without downtime.

others.B: ElastiCache speeds up reads, not heavy writes, and querying the cache does not relieve write pressure.
others.C: DocumentDB is a MongoDB-compatible document store and would require rewriting a MySQL application.
others.D: EFS is a file system, not a relational database for MySQL.

tip: Write-heavy relational workloads needing consistent IOPS mean Provisioned IOPS (io1/io2). gp3 lets you set IOPS independently at lower cost.

why: Client-side encryption in the application, for example with the AWS Encryption SDK or S3 Encryption Client using a KMS key, encrypts files before they leave the application. Only ciphertext is sent to and stored in S3, so no third party, AWS included, sees plaintext before encryption.

others.A: Client-side encryption with an S3 managed key is not a valid combination; S3 managed keys are used only server-side.
others.B: SSE-KMS encrypts only after the data arrives at S3, so it travels as plaintext (inside TLS) and is handled by AWS before encryption.
others.C: DSSE-KMS is still server-side and encrypts only after S3 receives the data.

tip: Encrypted before it reaches AWS means client-side encryption.

why: RDS automated backups take a daily snapshot plus transaction logs. Their retention can be set from the default 7 days up to 35 days, so changing it to 30 days meets the requirement with a single setting and no scripts.

others.A: A custom Lambda snapshot function needs code and cleanup logic for 30-day retention, which is more overhead.
others.C: Using Maintenance Windows to change retention is unnecessary indirection; you can just modify the setting once.
others.D: Manual daily CLI snapshots are operational toil and are not deleted automatically after 30 days.

tip: RDS automated backup retention ranges from 0 to 35 days. Longer retention needs manual snapshots or AWS Backup.

why: Adding an Aurora Replica to the existing cluster shares the same storage volume, so there is no data copying. Routing read-only queries to the reader endpoint and writes to the cluster (writer) endpoint offloads read traffic so write performance recovers. This is the cheapest scaling path.

others.A: A second cluster plus a copy job duplicates storage and adds replication lag and complexity.
others.B: DAX works only with DynamoDB, not Aurora.
others.D: Redshift is for analytics, and copying data there costs more and is unsuitable for application reads.

tip: Reads slowing writes in Aurora means add Aurora Replicas and use the reader endpoint.

why: Amazon Data Firehose is serverless, scales automatically for streaming ingestion, and buffers the incoming data. ECS on AWS Fargate runs the 30-minute processing job in serverless containers that scale out with load and have no time limit. Together they form a scalable, serverless pipeline.

others.B: Lambda functions are limited to 15 minutes, so a 30-minute job cannot run in one function, and splitting it adds complexity.
others.C: DMS migrates databases and does not ingest streaming application data.
others.D: EC2 Auto Scaling groups are not serverless and require server management.

tip: Jobs over 15 minutes in serverless architectures mean Fargate (or AWS Batch on Fargate).

why: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint adds a prefix-list route so EC2 traffic to S3 stays on the AWS network and never crosses the public internet. Endpoint and bucket policies can further restrict access, which suits sensitive data.

others.B: NLBs cannot target S3 buckets; targets must be instances, IPs, ALBs or Lambda.
others.C: S3 buckets are regional services and cannot be deployed inside a VPC.
others.D: Direct Connect links on-premises networks to AWS, not a VPC to S3.

tip: VPC to S3 privately means a gateway endpoint (or an interface endpoint when on-premises access is needed).

why: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes CloudWatch utilization metrics for EBS volumes and recommends better volume types, sizes, IOPS or throughput, for example gp2 to gp3. It also shows the estimated monthly savings opportunity for each recommendation.

others.A: Inspector assesses vulnerabilities, not cost optimization.
others.B: Systems Manager handles operations and inventory but does not produce EBS cost recommendations with savings estimates.
others.C: CloudWatch provides raw metrics only, with no optimization recommendations or savings estimates.

tip: Right-sizing recommendations with savings estimates for EC2, EBS, Lambda, ECS on Fargate or RDS come from Compute Optimizer.

why: S3 Storage Lens gives organization-wide, cross-Region visibility of S3 usage and activity. Its data-protection metrics, such as versioning-enabled bucket counts, show which buckets lack versioning, with no scanning or scripting needed.

others.C: IAM Access Analyzer for S3 finds buckets shared publicly or across accounts; it does not report versioning status.
others.D: Multi-Region Access Points route requests to buckets in several Regions and do not identify configuration such as versioning.

tip: AWS Config rule s3-bucket-versioning-enabled is another way to detect this. Storage Lens gives a dashboard view across accounts and Regions.

why: SQS FIFO queues provide exactly-once processing through deduplication IDs within a 5-minute window, and they keep order per message group. The queue absorbs unpredictable surges by decoupling order intake from Lambda processing, so customers are not affected.

others.B: SNS standard topics have at-least-once delivery, so duplicates are possible, and there is no buffering for consumers.
others.C: AppFlow is for SaaS data integration, not transactional order queueing.
others.D: X-Ray is for tracing and CloudWatch is for monitoring; neither is an order queue.

tip: Exactly-once plus buffering surges means SQS FIFO (high-throughput mode for higher TPS).

why: The role must live in the account that owns the resources (Production), with a trust policy that trusts the Development account. Development admins then allow only selected developers (two at first, more later) to call sts:AssumeRole on it. Access grows by updating permissions in Development, without creating users in Production.

others.A: Creating separate policies and users in each account duplicates identities and does not give cross-account access.
others.B: A role in Development cannot grant permissions to Production resources; the role must be in the target account.
others.D: IAM groups cannot be principals in a trust policy.

tip: Cross-account access means the role sits in the target (resource) account and trusts the source account.

why: Amazon Cognito provides serverless, scalable user authentication that issues JWTs. Lambda@Edge runs authorization checks on those tokens at CloudFront edge locations close to users for low latency. CloudFront serves the web application globally, and all three services scale with a growing user base.

others.B: Managed Microsoft AD is not serverless or designed for customer logins, and an ALB is regional, not global delivery.
others.C: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads to S3; it is not a global content delivery or authorization layer.
others.D: Managed Microsoft AD is not serverless customer identity, and Elastic Beanstalk is regional, not global delivery.

tip: Global, low-latency authorization at the edge means CloudFront plus Lambda@Edge (or CloudFront Functions) with Cognito tokens.

why: An SCP in AWS Organizations, attached to the accounts or their OU, can deny ec2:RunInstances when the ec2:InstanceType condition matches large types. It applies to every principal in those accounts, including admins, from one central policy, so overhead is lowest.

others.A: Updating IAM policies for every user in every account takes more effort and can be bypassed by admins.
others.B: AWS RAM shares resources; it does not restrict instance launches.
others.C: A deny role is ineffective, because developers can still launch through their own permissions without assuming it.

tip: Guardrails across many accounts mean SCPs (with conditions such as ec2:InstanceType or aws:RequestedRegion).

why: Systems Manager Patch Manager and Inventory automate OS updates and software inventory across mixed Windows Server versions and Linux distributions. Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances for software CVEs, and its findings can be exported as reports, giving each instance's vulnerability summary for monthly reviews.

others.A: Security Hub aggregates findings but does not scan instances for CVEs itself; it depends on Inspector for that.
others.C: Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks, and AWS Config does not install patches.
others.D: GuardDuty detects threats rather than listing vulnerabilities, and Config does not apply patches.

tip: Patching means Systems Manager Patch Manager. CVE scanning means Inspector.

why: A warm standby keeps an Auto Scaling group and ELB already running in the DR Region. DynamoDB global tables replicate data across Regions in about a second, and Route 53 DNS failover with health checks switches traffic automatically. With everything pre-provisioned, downtime is lowest.

others.B: Launching all resources, including DynamoDB tables, from CloudFormation at failover time takes much longer and the data would not be replicated.
